supports.excerpt:
If the `watchType` is set to `FileProcessingMode.PROCESS_CONTINUOUSLY`, when a file is modified, its contents are re-processed entirely. This can break the “exactly-once” semantics, as appending data at the end of a file will lead to all its contents being re-processed.

-

Socket-based:

- `socketTextStream` - Reads from a socket. Elements can be separated by a delimiter.

Collection-based:

-

`fromCollection(Collection)` - Creates a data stream from the Java Java.util.Collection. All elements
in the collection must be of the same type.

-

`fromCollection(Iterator, Class)` - Creates a data stream from an iterator. The class specifies the
data type of the elements returned by the iterator.

-

`fromElements(T ...)` - Creates a data stream from the given sequence of objects. All objects must be
of the same type.

-

`fromParallelCollection(SplittableIterator, Class)` - Creates a data stream from an iterator, in
parallel. The class specifies the data type of the elements returned by the iterator.

-

`generateSequence(from, to)` - Generates the sequence of numbers in the given interval, in
parallel.

Custom:

- `addSource` - Attach a new source function. For example, to read from Apache Kafka you can use
`addSource(new FlinkKafkaConsumer<>(...))`. See connectors for more details.

skill_drafts.name: File-based Data Source Configuration
skill_drafts.description: Configure and instantiate file-based data sources in Flink DataStream API, supporting text files and custom input formats. Handles continuous file monitoring with explicit awareness of exactly-once semantics constraints.
skill_drafts.objective: Set up file-based streaming data ingestion
applicable_signals: File path and format parameters available
contraindications: Source is collection-based (use fromCollection, fromElements, or generateSequence)
Source requires custom connector such as Kafka (use addSource with appropriate consumer)
Exactly-once semantics is critical and file modification is expected during execution
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Determine file source type', 'detail': 'Identify whether source is text file or requires custom InputFormat'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Select configuration method', 'detail': 'Use readTextFile(path) for text files or readFile(fileInputFormat, path) for custom formats'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Configure watchType if continuous monitoring needed', 'detail': 'Set watchType parameter; if FileProcessingMode.PROCESS_CONTINUOUSLY, acknowledge exactly-once breakage risk'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Attach source to StreamExecutionEnvironment', 'detail': 'Invoke configured method on environment instance to create DataStream'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Verify DataStream readiness', 'detail': 'Confirm DataStream object is created and ready for downstream operations'}
triggers: Streaming application requires reading from local or distributed file systems
Data source is text-based or uses custom InputFormat
File-based ingestion is the primary data entry point
constraints: All elements in a collection-based source must be of the same type
FileProcessingMode.PROCESS_CONTINUOUSLY re-processes entire file contents on modification, breaking exactly-once guarantees
File must respect TextInputFormat specification for readTextFile method
cautions: Appending data to a file with PROCESS_CONTINUOUSLY mode causes all prior contents to be re-processed
Exactly-once semantics cannot be guaranteed when using continuous file monitoring with file modifications
output_contract: Configured DataStream object with file source attached, watchType parameter set appropriately, and ready for downstream transformations or actions

metadata.prompt:
To set up a file-based data source:
1. Choose the appropriate method: readTextFile(path) for text files, or readFile(fileInputFormat, path) for custom formats.
2. If continuous monitoring is required, set watchType to FileProcessingMode.PROCESS_CONTINUOUSLY, but understand this breaks exactly-once semantics when files are appended.
3. Attach the configured source to the StreamExecutionEnvironment.
4. Verify the resulting DataStream is ready for downstream transformations.

skill_drafts.name: Collection-based Data Source Creation
skill_drafts.description: Create DataStream objects from in-memory Java collections, iterators, or element sequences with type consistency enforcement. Use this skill to initialize streaming data from local collections or programmatically generated sequences for testing, reference datasets, or small homogeneous data sources.
skill_drafts.objective: Initialize streaming data from local collections or sequences
applicable_signals: Test data or small reference datasets need to be streamed
Programmatically generated sequences or in-memory collections are available
Local initialization phase before streaming operators
contraindications: Data volume is large or unbounded
Source is external (files, sockets, message queues, Kafka)
Runtime data generation or continuous streaming from external systems is required
intervention_moves: Select collection-based source method matching data structure (Collection, Iterator, varargs, or sequence)
Validate type consistency across all elements
Capture returned DataStream for downstream use
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Identify data source type', 'detail': 'Determine whether data is a Collection, Iterator, varargs sequence, or numeric range'}

{'step': 2, 'action': 'Select appropriate method', 'detail': 'Choose fromCollection(Collection), fromCollection(Iterator, Class), fromElements(T ...), fromParallelCollection(SplittableIterator, Class), or generateSequence(from, to)'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Verify type homogeneity', 'detail': 'Ensure all elements are of the same type; specify type class if using Iterator variant'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Invoke on StreamExecutionEnvironment', 'detail': 'Call the selected method to create DataStream'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Validate output', 'detail': 'Confirm DataStream is populated and ready for downstream operators'}
triggers: Test data, small reference datasets, or programmatically generated sequences need to be streamed; all elements are homogeneous type
constraints: All elements in the collection or sequence must be of the same type
Collection must be fully materialized in memory
Iterator-based sources require explicit type class specification
cautions: Collection-based sources are suitable for testing and small datasets only; avoid for production large-scale data
Type mismatch will cause runtime errors; verify type consistency before invocation
output_contract: DataStream object populated with collection or iterator elements, type-safe and ready for downstream operators (map, filter, window, sink, etc.)

examples.output: DataStream<Integer> with 5 elements, ready for map/filter operations
examples.notes: Use fromCollection(Collection) for standard Java collections

examples.input: Iterator over strings with type class String.class
examples.notes: Use fromCollection(Iterator, Class) when data is iterator-based

examples.output: DataStream<Long> with sequence 1 to 100 generated in parallel
examples.notes: Use generateSequence for numeric sequences; parallel execution by default

metadata.prompt:
To create a DataStream from a collection-based source:
1. Choose the appropriate method based on your data structure:
   - fromCollection(Collection): Pass a Java Collection; all elements must be the same type.
   - fromCollection(Iterator, Class): Pass an Iterator and specify the element type class.
   - fromElements(T ...): Pass a varargs sequence of objects; all must be the same type.
   - fromParallelCollection(SplittableIterator, Class): Pass a SplittableIterator for parallel creation.
   - generateSequence(from, to): Generate a numeric sequence in parallel.
2. Ensure type homogeneity: all elements in the collection or sequence must be of the same type.
3. Invoke the method on StreamExecutionEnvironment to obtain a DataStream object.
4. The returned DataStream is ready for downstream operators (map, filter, window, etc.).

skill_drafts.name: Continuous File Monitoring Semantics Constraint
skill_drafts.description: Enforce exactly-once semantics awareness when using FileProcessingMode.PROCESS_CONTINUOUSLY. Flag and validate the risk that full file re-processing on modification breaks exactly-once delivery guarantees.
skill_drafts.objective: Prevent unintended exactly-once semantics violation in continuous file monitoring
applicable_signals: File source initialization or reconfiguration event
contraindications: File source is not used in the pipeline
At-least-once or best-effort semantics is explicitly acceptable
Files are immutable after initial write (no append or modification expected)
intervention_moves: Detect watchType=PROCESS_CONTINUOUSLY in file source config
Query application semantics requirement (exactly-once vs. at-least-once vs. best-effort)
If exactly-once required and continuous mode active: log warning and recommend mode switch or semantics relaxation
Optionally block source initialization if conflict is unresolved
triggers: File-based source is configured with watchType=PROCESS_CONTINUOUSLY; application requires exactly-once delivery guarantee
constraints: Must validate watchType setting before source activation
Must check declared semantics guarantee against file monitoring mode
Configuration validation must occur at setup time, not runtime
cautions: Appending data to a monitored file triggers full re-processing of all prior contents
File modifications (not just appends) trigger complete file re-read
This constraint applies only to PROCESS_CONTINUOUSLY mode; PROCESS_ONCE mode is safe for exactly-once
output_contract: Configuration validated or rejected with explicit status. If conflict detected: warning logged and configuration flagged for review. If compatible: validation passes silently. Caller receives boolean pass/fail and optional diagnostic message.

examples.input: File source with watchType=PROCESS_CONTINUOUSLY; application semantics=EXACTLY_ONCE
examples.output: Validation fails. Warning: 'Continuous file monitoring breaks exactly-once semantics. Switch to PROCESS_ONCE or accept at-least-once delivery.'
examples.notes: Conflict detected; configuration rejected or flagged for manual override.

examples.input: File source with watchType=PROCESS_CONTINUOUSLY; application semantics=AT_LEAST_ONCE
examples.notes: Semantics are compatible; continuous monitoring is safe.

examples.input: File source with watchType=PROCESS_ONCE; application semantics=EXACTLY_ONCE

metadata.prompt: When a file-based source is configured with watchType=PROCESS_CONTINUOUSLY, validate that the application's semantics requirement is compatible. If exactly-once delivery is required, warn or reject the configuration: continuous file monitoring will re-process entire file contents when modified, violating exactly-once semantics. Appending data to a file triggers full re-processing of all prior contents.
